exercises.title: Rock a Bye Baby
exercises.instructions:
Rock-a-bye baby on the tree top,
When the wind blows the cradle will rock.
If the bow breaks the cradle will fall,
We will catch baby cradle and all.
Sit and sing the rhyme together rocking a pretend baby backwards and forwards.
Stand up and be a tall tree. Wave your branches in the wind. High, low, to the front and behind.
Swing both arms from side to side stretching out as far as you can. (x 3)
Swing forwards and backwards reaching out to the front and behind. (x 3)
Stretch up high, turn around. Stop arms by your side and count to 3.
Stretch up high and turn the other way. Stop arms by your side and count to 3.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty standing tall, moving arms in different directions, coordinating swings, turning safely, and maintaining balance when stopping.
Completes some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can move arms and attempt turns but movements may be limited, uncoordinated, or affect balance. Able to stop briefly after turning.

Completes most of the sequence independently. Uses a good range of arm movements, performs both arm swings with some control, stretches upwards effectively, turns in both directions, and regains balance after stopping.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed posture, balance, and coordination. Demonstrates full range of movement in all directions, controlled arm swings, effective stretching, smooth turns both ways, and maintains stillness while counting to three.

exercises.title: See Saw Marjory Daw
exercises.instructions:
See saw Marjory Daw (Move hands up and down the make the see saw)
Johnny just wants to go faster.
Up and down as fast as you can. (Both hands up and down)
Try not to end in disaster. (Shake index finger)
Sit on the floor. Sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Stand up and sing the song doing the following actions:
See saw Marjory Daw (Stretch up)
Johnny just wants to go faster. (Crouch down)
Up and down as fast as you can. (Stretch up and down)
Try not to end in disaster. (Shake index finger)
Lie on your front, head to the side, eyes closed.
Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty standing tall, moving arms in different directions, coordinating swings, turning safely, and maintaining balance when stopping.
Completes some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can move arms and attempt turns but movements may be limited, uncoordinated, or affect balance. Able to stop briefly after turning.

Completes most of the sequence independently. Uses a good range of arm movements, performs both arm swings with some control, stretches upwards effectively, turns in both directions, and regains balance after stopping.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed posture, balance, and coordination. Demonstrates full range of movement in all directions, controlled arm swings, effective stretching, smooth turns both ways, and maintains stillness while counting to three.

exercises.title: Ride A Strong Horse
exercises.instructions:
Ride a strong horse through high wind and snows. (Pretend to hold the reins and move arms round as if riding a horse)
To gift a fine lady a beautiful rose.
Rings on her fingers and bells on her toes, (Hold hands up and shake fingers, wiggle toes)
She shall have music wherever she goes. (Conduct to music – both hands, pointed fingers).
Sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Sit on the floor. Click your tongue on the roof of your mouth to make a galloping sound.
Gallop around the room one way and then the other.
Be still, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying actions, coordinating movements with the rhyme, producing the galloping sound, moving safely around the space, or remaining still at the end.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can copy simple actions and attempt galloping movements but coordination, balance, rhythm, or spatial awareness may be inconsistent. Attempts to remain still for the count of five.

Completes most of the activity independently. Coordinates actions with the rhyme, performs the galloping sound and movement with reasonable control, changes direction successfully, and remains still for most of the counting activity.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, balance, rhythm, and body control. Accurately matches actions to the rhyme, gallops confidently in both directions, demonstrates good awareness of space, and remains calm and still with eyes closed for the full count of five.

exercises.title: Once I Caught A Fish Alive
exercises.instructions:
One, two, three four five. (Hold up fingers and thumb)
Once I caught a fish alive. (Point and shake finger)
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten. (Hold up other fingers and thumb)
Then I let him go again. (Make fish wiggling away with one hand)
Why did you let him go? (Hold out hands)
Because he bit my finger so. (Point and shake finger – other hand)
Which finger did he bite? (Hold out hands)
This little finger on the right! (Wiggle little finger)
Sit and sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Stand up wiggle like a slippery fish.
Open and close your mouth wide like a large fish.
Wiggle one little finger.
Wiggle the other little finger.
Wiggle both little fingers together.
Pretend to swim like a fish around the room in different directions.
Stop. Lie on your back. Imagine you are a fish under water. Blow bubbles to the surface.
Close your eyes. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying finger actions, isolating little finger movements, coordinating actions with the rhyme, moving around the space safely, or engaging in the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can copy simple hand and finger movements and attempt fish actions, but coordination, finger control, movement quality, or spatial awareness may be inconsistent. Attempts to relax and follow the countdown.

Completes most of the activity independently. Coordinates hand and finger actions with the rhyme, demonstrates good body awareness during fish movements, swims around the space appropriately, and participates in the relaxation activity with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, finger isolation, body control, spatial awareness, and concentration. Accurately performs all rhyme actions, controls movements while travelling around the room, and relaxes calmly throughout the countdown.

exercises.title: Polly Put the Kettle On
exercises.instructions:
Start with hands clasped into a fist on chest – thumb on top.
Polly put the kettle on. (Stretch out arm to front make a starfish and return)
Polly put the kettle on. (Stretch the other arm out to the front to make a starfish and back)
Polly put the kettle on. (Stretch both arms out to make a starfish and back.)
We'll all have tea. (Stretch both arms out)
Start with hands clasped into a fist on chest – thumb on top
Susan take it off again. (Stretch out arm to front make a starfish and return)
Susan take it off again. (Stretch the other arm out to the front to make a starfish and back)
Susan take it off again. (Stretch both arms out to make a starfish and back.)
They've all gone away. (Wave goodbye)
Sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Stretch your fingers (splay)
Make a fist. (Thumb on top)
Stand feet slightly apart – stretch arms up high – look at the ceiling and then look down. Repeat 3 times.
Stand feet slightly apart. Stretch arms out to the sides at shoulder height and lift them up and down. Repeat 3 times.
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying hand and arm movements, opening and closing the hands, coordinating actions with the rhyme, changing head position, or following the relaxation sequence.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can imitate simple arm and hand movements but range of movement, coordination, finger control, or attention may be inconsistent. Attempts the relaxation activity with encouragement.

Completes most of the activity independently. Coordinates actions with the rhyme, demonstrates good hand opening and closing, performs overhead and side arm movements with reasonable control, and remains calm during the countdown.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, body control, and attention. Accurately performs all hand and arm actions, demonstrates full range of movement, follows positional changes smoothly, and relaxes quietly throughout the countdown.

exercises.title: Ring a Ring of Roses
exercises.instructions:
Ring a ring of roses
A pocket full of posies.
A-tish-oo, A-tish-oo
We all fall down.
Roses in the garden.
Blossom on the tree.
We all jump up with a one, two, three.
Hold hands and sing the rhyme together going around in a circle. Crouch down on the last line of verse one. Jump up on the last line of verse 2.
Make big circles in front of you with one arm – one way and then the other. Now make circles with the other arm.
Make circles to the side – one way and then the other.
Use your other arm to make circles to the side – one way and then the other.
Imagine there is a small hole in front of you. Walk around the hole – one way and then the other. Make the hole bigger – jump around the hole and back again. Jump over the hole and lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty moving in a circle with others, following the rhyme actions, coordinating arm circles, jumping activities, or transitioning to the resting position.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt circle movements, crouching, jumping and arm circles, but balance, coordination, timing or spatial awareness may be inconsistent. Requires reminders to rest quietly.

Completes most of the activity independently. Moves around the circle with others, performs crouching and jumping actions with reasonable control, makes arm circles in different directions, and demonstrates good awareness of the imaginary obstacle. Settles for the rest period with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, balance, rhythm, and spatial awareness. Accurately follows all actions within the rhyme, controls arm movements in all directions, safely negotiates the imaginary obstacle, performs jumps confidently, and relaxes quietly for the full count of five.

exercises.title: Five Little Ducks
exercises.instructions:
Five little ducks went swimming one day. (Hold-up 5 )
Over the hill and far away. (Use hand and arm to make hill)
Mother duck said, "Quack, quack, quack, quack," (Use hand to 'quack)
But only four little ducks came back. (Hold-up 4)
Repeat for four, three, two, one.
When the one little duck goes swimming one day the last line is 'and all her five little ducks came back'.
Sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Turn your head slowly from side to side (pretend you are looking for the ducklings).
Nod your head forwards and backwards (Yes, you can see the ducklings).
Walk around the duck pond
Turn and walk back around the other way.
Spread your toes to make webbed feet. Paddle across the duck pond.
Stand straight – use your arms to flap like wings.
Use your hands to make a beak – open and close one at a time and then together.
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying hand actions, showing number fingers, moving the head in different directions, walking safely around the space, coordinating duck movements, or settling for the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt finger actions, head movements, walking and paddling actions, but coordination, balance, body awareness, or attention may be inconsistent. Requires reminders to remain still during relaxation.

Completes most of the activity independently. Uses fingers accurately for counting, performs duck actions with reasonable coordination, changes direction successfully while walking, and participates appropriately in the relaxation activity with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, balance, body control, and attention. Accurately performs finger counting, duck beak actions, head movements, walking and paddling activities, demonstrates strong spatial awareness throughout, and relaxes quietly for the full countdown.

exercises.title: Humpty Dumpty
exercises.instructions:
Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall.
Humpty Dumpty had a great fall.
All the King's horses and all the King's men,
Put Humpty Dumpty together again.
Sing the rhyme together.
Stretch up tall to touch the top of the wall.
Walk along the wall in a straight line – careful not to fall!
Now walk backward along the wall.
Pretend to sit on the wall. Sing the song again.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty stretching upwards, walking along a straight line, walking backwards safely, maintaining balance, or moving between standing, sitting and lying positions.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt stretching, line walking and role-play actions, but balance, coordination, posture or confidence may be inconsistent. Requires reminders during the resting activity.

Completes most of the activity independently. Maintains balance for much of the line walking task, walks backwards with reasonable control, joins in with the rhyme and role-play elements, and rests quietly with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed balance, coordination and body control. Walks forwards and backwards along the line accurately, demonstrates strong postural control during stretching and pretend sitting activities, follows all instructions, and remains calm and relaxed throughout the rest period.

exercises.title: Pussy Cat, Pussy Cat
exercises.instructions:
Pussy cat, pussy cat where have you been?
I've been to London to visit the Queen.
Pussy cat, pussy cat pussy cat what was there?
I found a small mouse right under her chair.
Pussy cat, pussy cat where are you now?
In front of the Queen and giving a bow.
Pussy cat, pussy cat what did she think?
She smiled down at me and gave me a wink.
Stretch like a cat.
Crawl around the room like a cat.
Scamper like a mouse.
Walk like a king or queen around the room.
Stretch up high and bow down low (x 3)
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying animal movements, moving safely around the space, changing body positions, stretching and bowing, or engaging in the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt cat crawling, mouse scampering and king or queen walking, but balance, coordination, body awareness or movement control may be inconsistent. Requires reminders to follow instructions and settle during relaxation.

Completes most of the activity independently. Demonstrates appropriate animal movements, moves around the space with reasonable control, performs stretching and bowing actions accurately, and participates in the relaxation activity with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, balance, body control and imagination. Successfully adapts movement styles for different characters, moves safely and confidently around the space, performs stretches and bows with control, and remains calm and relaxed throughout the countdown.

exercises.title: Round and Round the Garden
exercises.instructions:
Round and round the garden, (Use pointy finger to go around and around palm of hand.)
Like a teddy bear.
One step, two step and (Use pointy finger to do three steps up the arm.)
Tickle you under there! (Tickle under arm.)
Sing the song doing the actions.
Repeat using other hand.
March around the garden like a teddy bear. One way and then the other.
Growl like a teddy bear.
Use your paws to claw the air like a bear. High, in the middle and down low.
Imagine you are watching the bear. Stand very still arms by your side. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty copying hand actions, isolating finger movements, coordinating bear actions, moving around the space safely, standing still, or participating in the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt finger tracing, marching and bear movements, but coordination, body awareness, balance or attention may be inconsistent. Requires reminders to remain still and follow instructions.

Completes most of the activity independently. Demonstrates reasonable finger control during the rhyme, marches in both directions with control, performs bear actions appropriately, stands still for most of the count, and participates in relaxation with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, balance, body control and concentration. Accurately performs all hand and finger actions, moves confidently in different directions, varies bear movements at different heights, maintains stillness for the full count, and relaxes calmly throughout the countdown.

exercises.title: Wind the Bobbin Up
exercises.instructions:
Wind the bobbin up.
Wind the bobbin up.
Pull, pull, clap, clap, clap.
Wind it back again,
Wind it back again.
Pull, pull, clap, clap, clap.
Point to the ceiling, point to the floor.
Point to the window, point to the door.
Clap your hands together 1, 2, 3.
Put your hands upon your knee.
Sing the rhyme together doing the actions.
Roll your arms over and over each other as fast as you can. Forward and backward.
Lie on the floor and clasp your hands above your head,
Roll over and over one way and then back again.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty coordinating hand actions, clapping, pointing accurately, rolling arms continuously, performing floor rolling activities, or settling for the rest period.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt the rhyme actions and rolling movements but coordination, body awareness, balance, or movement sequencing may be inconsistent. Requires reminders during the relaxation activity.

Completes most of the activity independently. Coordinates the majority of actions with the rhyme, points accurately to different locations, rolls arms and body with reasonable control, and participates in the rest activity with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, rhythm, body control, and spatial awareness. Accurately matches movements to the rhyme, demonstrates smooth arm and body rolling movements, follows instructions consistently, and relaxes quietly throughout the count to five.

exercises.title: The Farmer's in the Field
exercises.instructions:
The farmer's in the field. The farmer sees a cow,
The farmer's in the field. The farmer sees a cow.
A, E, I, O, U, A, E, I, O, U,
The farmer's in the field. The farmer sees a cow.
The farmer sees a sheep. The farmer sees a duck.
The farmer sees a sheep. The farmer sees a duck.
A, E, I, O, U, A, E, I, O, U,
The farmer sees a sheep. The farmer sees a duck.
The farmer sees a dog. We all pat the dog.
The farmer sees a dog. We all pat the dog.
A, E, I, O, U, A, E, I, O, U,
The farmer sees a dog. We all pat the dog.
Form a circle and sing the song. At the end of each verse make the sound of the animal. On the last verse everyone be the dog and pat themselves.
Lie down on your back and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty joining the circle, following the song, copying animal sounds or actions, participating with others, or settling for the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can join in with some animal sounds, actions or vowel sounds, but attention, confidence, coordination or group participation may be inconsistent. Requires reminders during the relaxation activity.

Completes most of the activity independently. Joins in with the song, copies most animal sounds and actions appropriately, participates within the group circle, and rests quietly with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed listening, participation and self-control. Joins in confidently with the song, animal sounds, vowel sounds and actions, demonstrates awareness of others within the circle, and relaxes calmly throughout the count to five.

exercises.title: Five Fat Sausages
exercises.instructions:
Five fat sausages sizzling in a pan. (Shake your body.)
One went pop and the other went bang! (Stretch one arm out to the front and then the other – spread your fingers like a starfish.)
Four fat sausages sizzling in a pan. (Shake your body.)
One went pop and the other went bang! (Stretch one arm to the ceiling and then the other one.)
Three fat sausages sitting in a pan. (Shake your body.)
One went pop and the other went bang! (Stretch one arm towards the floor and then the other one.)
Two fat sausages sitting in a pan. (Shake your body.)
One went pop and the other went bang! (Stretch one arm out to the side and then the other one.)
One fat sausage sitting in a pan. (Shake your body.)
It went pop and it went bang. (Stretch one arm behind you and then the other one.)
No fat sausages sitting in a pan. (Shake your head.)
No more pop and no more bang! (Wag finger from side to side.)
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Requires significant support to participate. Has difficulty coordinating body shaking, reaching in different directions, extending arms fully, copying finger and head movements, or settling for the relaxation activity.

Participates in some parts of the activity with prompts or support. Can attempt body shaking and arm stretches but movement accuracy, coordination, range of movement or body awareness may be inconsistent. Requires reminders to follow the sequence and settle during rest time.

Completes most of the activity independently. Demonstrates a good range of movement when reaching in different directions, coordinates body and arm actions with the rhyme, follows the countdown sequence, and participates in the relaxation activity with minimal prompting.

Completes the entire sequence independently with well-developed coordination, body control and attention. Accurately performs all directional reaches, body shaking, finger and head movements, demonstrates strong awareness of body position in space, and relaxes quietly throughout the count to five.

exercises.title: If You're Happy and You Know It
exercises.instructions:
If you're happy and you know it clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it and you really want to show it.
If you're happy and you know it,
Clap your hands.
Repeat: Stamp your feet
Sing the song together doing the actions.
Clap your hands high then low.
Clap your hands to the side and then the other side.
Clap your hands in front and now behind.
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with a few actions but needs significant support to clap hands, stamp feet, change levels (high and low), move arms to the sides, clap in front and behind, and settle quietly lying on their back.

Attempts most actions including clapping, stamping, and moving hands high, low, to the sides, in front and behind. May lose rhythm, coordination, or need reminders to follow the sequence and lie still at the end.

Completes most of the actions in time with the song. Claps and stamps with control, changes direction and level appropriately, follows the sequence with only minor errors, and lies quietly with eyes closed while counting back.

Performs all actions confidently and accurately in time with the song. Claps high, low, to both sides, in front and behind with good coordination, stamps feet rhythmically, follows the complete sequence independently, and relaxes calmly while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Here We Go Round the Mulberry Bush
exercises.instructions:
Here we go round the mulberry bush,
The mulberry bush, the mulberry bush.
Here we go round the mulberry bush,
On a cold and frosty morning.
This is the way we wash our hands,
Wash our hands, wash our hands.
This is the way we wash our hands,
On a cold and frosty morning.
This is the way we comb our hair,
Comb our hair, comb our hair.
This is the way we comb our hair,
On a cold and frosty morning.
This is the way we brush our teeth.
Brush our teeth, brush our teeth.
This is the way we brush our teeth,
On a cold and frosty morning.
This is the way we say, "Goodbye,"
Say, "Goodbye," say, "Goodbye."
This is the way we say, "Goodbye,"
On a cold and frosty morning.
Sing the song together doing the actions. Use other ideas e.g. 'This is the way we put on our clothes'.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some of the song and attempts a few actions such as washing hands, combing hair, brushing teeth, or waving goodbye. Needs significant support to follow the sequence, move around the circle, and settle to rest on their tummy.

Attempts most of the actions and joins in with moving around the circle. Can imitate washing hands, combing hair, brushing teeth, and saying goodbye but may need reminders to follow the order of actions and rest quietly at the end.

Follows the song and performs most actions correctly. Moves around the circle with control, demonstrates self-care actions clearly, responds well to additional action ideas, and lies quietly on their tummy while counting to 5 with minimal support.

Performs all actions confidently and accurately in time with the song. Moves smoothly around the circle, clearly demonstrates washing hands, combing hair, brushing teeth, saying goodbye, and other suggested actions, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly to rest on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes
exercises.instructions:
Head, shoulders, knees and toes,
Knees and toes.
Head, shoulders, knees and toes.
Knees and toes.
Eyes and ears and mouth and nose.
Head, shoulders, knees and toes,
Knees and toes.
Sing the song together doing the actions
Touch your ear. Now touch the other ear.
Touch your nose.
Touch your elbow. Now touch your other elbow.
Nod your head slowly forwards and backwards.
Now slowly shake your head from side to side.
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some of the song and attempts to touch a few body parts. Needs significant support to identify head, shoulders, knees, toes, ears, nose and elbows, follow the actions, and settle quietly lying on their back.

Identifies and touches most body parts when prompted and attempts the head movements. May need reminders to follow the sequence, touch the correct body part, or maintain control when nodding and shaking the head.

Correctly touches most body parts in time with the song, including ears, nose and elbows. Performs the nodding and side-to-side head movements with control, follows the sequence with minimal support, and relaxes quietly while counting back from 5.

Independently and accurately touches all named body parts during the song and additional actions. Demonstrates well-developed body awareness, performs head movements smoothly and safely, follows the complete sequence in time with the music, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Mr Thumb
exercises.instructions:
Mr Thumb, Mr Thumb,
Where are you?
Here I am, here I am.
How do you do?
Mrs Pointer, Mrs Pointer,
Where are you?
Here I am, here I am.
How do you do?
Doctor Tall, Doctor Tall,
Where are you?
Here I am, Here I am.
How do you do?
Madam Ring, Madam Ring,
Where are you?
Here I am, here I am.
How do you do?
Baby small, baby small,
Where are you?
Here I am, here I am.
How do you do?
Sing the song together. On 'here I am' raise the correct thumb or finger. On the second 'here I am' raise the other thumb or finger and bow to each other for 'How do you do?'
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with parts of the song but needs significant support to identify and raise the correct thumb or finger, coordinate both hands, bow appropriately, and settle to rest on their tummy.

Attempts to raise the correct thumb and fingers during the song and joins in with the bowing action. May confuse some fingers, require reminders, or need support to coordinate movements and follow the sequence.

Correctly identifies and raises most thumbs and fingers at the appropriate time, uses both hands with reasonable coordination, bows during "How do you do?" and follows the sequence with minimal support. Rests quietly on their tummy while counting to 5.

Independently identifies and raises the correct thumb, pointer, middle, ring and little fingers on both hands in time with the song. Demonstrates well-developed finger control and coordination, bows appropriately during "How do you do?", follows the complete sequence accurately, and settles calmly on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Teddy Bear, Teddy Bear
exercises.instructions:
Teddy bear, teddy bear, turn around.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, touch the ground.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, reach up high.
Teddy bear, teddy bear touch the sky.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, bend down low.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, touch your toe.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, go to bed.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, rest your head.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, turn off the light.
Teddy bear, teddy bear say, "Goodnight."
Say the rhyme doing the actions.
Lie on your back, eyes closed.
Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some of the rhyme and attempts a few actions such as turning, reaching, bending or touching toes. Needs significant support to follow the sequence of movements, maintain balance, and settle quietly on their back at the end.

Attempts most actions including turning around, touching the ground, reaching high, bending low, touching toes, and pretending to go to bed. May need reminders to follow the order of the rhyme, control movements, or complete all actions independently.

Completes most actions correctly and in sequence. Demonstrates good control when turning, reaching, bending and touching toes, follows the story of the rhyme with minimal support, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5.

Performs all actions confidently and accurately in time with the rhyme. Turns around smoothly, touches the ground and toes, reaches high, bends low with control, acts out going to bed, resting their head, turning off the light and saying "Goodnight" independently, then settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.
